extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants, agents, and attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, issuing, replying to, and processing requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105, and related Patentability Report practice. Covers what must be included in requirements, what constitutes a complete/good-faith reply, timing, examiner obligations, and when Patentability Reports should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor and good faith for 1.105 replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to the applicant’s reply to a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, and requires that the applicant reply to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 with information reasonably and readily available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must respond with information that is reasonably and readily available; replies are subject to the same candor obligations as disclosures under 1.56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold distinction between 37 CFR 1.56 and 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.56 requires disclosure of information material to patentability; 37 CFR 1.105 permits the Office to require information reasonably necessary to examination (a substantially lower threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may require information beyond what applicant must disclose under 1.56 when reasonably necessary to determine state of the art, context, or similarity to other art; see Star Fruits example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant obligation limited to known/readily-available information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required by 37 CFR 1.105 to submit information already known, but there is no requirement to search for information that is unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must make a reasonable inquiry and good-faith attempt to obtain requested information, but is not required to perform investigation to find unknown material.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply to a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement giving either the information required or a statement that the information required is unknown and/or is not readily available to the party or parties from which it was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement to show information was not readily attainable, but applicant must make a good-faith attempt and reasonable inquiry. If information remains unknown after reasonable inquiry, applicant may simply state that it is 'unknown or not readily available.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity and adequacy of replies
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply stating the required information is unknown and/or not readily available will generally be sufficient unless it is clear the applicant did not understand the requirement or the reply was ambiguous and a more specific answer is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on surrounding facts, a reasonable follow-up requirement may be issued where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and consequences of an incomplete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement is handled like an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final Office action (see 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP § 714.03); form paragraph 7.95 may be used where the reply is bona fide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A TIME PERIOD of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS may be given to supply omission or correction to avoid abandonment; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a), except where deliberate omission occurred or application is subject to a final Office action (no extension if period expired).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply to 1.105 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies (or failures to reply) to 37 CFR 1.105 requirements are governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136. Requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months; applicant may extend up to six months under 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements sent with an Office action on the merits receive the same reply period as the action. A 1.105 requirement is an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 for patent term adjustment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow specification and scope of requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope because it burdens applicant and examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only warrant a requirement where the benefit from the information exceeds the burden of obtaining it; specify particular art area and claimed subject matter to avoid overly burdening applicant and avoid irrelevant volumes of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and content of a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement must clearly indicate that a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is being made, the basis for the requirement, and what information is being required, including the form expected (citations, collections, answers to questions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why the requirement is made and how the information is necessary to examination; specify scope, expected form, and particular art/classification details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for separate document for requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a requirement may be included within an Office action, it is generally prepared as a separate document so the recipient and those best able to respond are immediately alerted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate document is preferable for routing to parties best able to respond and for visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stipulations and interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs (e.g., 7.105.01, 7.105.02) should be used where the information pertains to stipulations of facts or interrogatories of facts known to the applicant; stipulations ask applicant to agree/disagree to factual assertions, interrogatories request answers to factual questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracketed instructions specify how to draft assertions/questions; scope of queries must be clearly set forth and expected replies characterized as factual information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Domain of Search (¶ 7.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to extend the domain of search for prior art: identify class/subclasses and describe why a broader range of art is necessary to establish the level of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when limited amounts of art are available within the Office and broader art is needed to assess knowledge of a person of ordinary skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: List of Keywords (¶ 7.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that applicant provide a list of keywords particularly helpful in locating publications related to the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert description of the art claimed but not found in classification system where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Level of Skill and Knowledge in the Art (¶ 7.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require information to document the level of skill and knowledge in the art of the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to establish the state of ordinary skill in the relevant art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Background Description (¶ 7.108)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require information to complete the background description in the disclosure by documenting specified aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to flesh out background and contextual material in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Products and Services Embodying Invention (¶ 7.109)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require identification of products and services embodying the disclosed subject matter and properties of similar products/services in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps demonstrate practical embodiments and compare to prior art products/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Citations for Electronically Searchable Databases (¶ 7.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request list of citations to electronically searchable databases or indexed collections containing publications documenting knowledge within the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and followed by closing paragraphs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Copy of Art Referred to in Disclosure But Not Submitted (¶ 7.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request copies of items of art referred to in the disclosure that were not previously submitted, describing where applicant referred to the art (specification, page, or paper received and page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually referred to in the disclosure; indicate specific locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Copies of Publications Authored by Inventor(s) (¶ 7.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request copies of each publication authored/co-authored by any of the applicants that describe the disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to place applicant-authored publications on record; limited to publications describing the disclosed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs: Art relied upon for various purposes (¶¶ 7.115–7.117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate requirements may ask for: (¶7.115) publications used as sources for the description of prior art (title, citation, copy, and concise explanation of contribution); (¶7.116) publications relied upon for development of the invention (title, citation, copy, concise explanation of reliance); (¶7.117) publications relied upon for drafting claimed subject matter (title, citation, copy, concise explanation of reliance in distinguishing claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each is limited to documents actually relied on (not merely believed relevant); include concise explanations of each publication's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Results of Applicant’s Prior Art Search (¶ 7.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require state whether any prior art search was performed; if so, list citations for each prior art collection searched and provide copies/citations of art considered material to demonstrating the knowledge of a person of ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify attributes of prior art that most closely approximate claimed subject matter to narrow focus of reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Details of Improvement Over the Prior Art (¶ 7.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require statement of specific improvements of the subject matter in claims over the disclosed prior art and indicate specific elements providing improvements; for means/steps-plus-function claims, provide specific page and line numbers in the disclosure describing structure/acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to substantiate distinctions over prior art and identify supporting portions of the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of only pertinent pages for large documents (¶ 7.122)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a requested document is a bound text or single article over 50 pages, the requirement may be met by providing copies of those pages that provide the particular subject matter indicated or the subject matter found in applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this provision where the scope specifically includes copies of publications to avoid unnecessary bulk submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fee and certification for initial reply (¶ 7.123)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 are waived for documents submitted in reply to this requirement if included in the applicant’s first complete communication responding to the requirement and within original time period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver extends only to documents within the scope of the requirement and included in the first complete communication; any supplemental communications or information beyond the scope are subject to 1.97/1.98 fees and certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a good faith reply (¶ 7.124)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies must be made with candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56; where applicant does not have or cannot readily obtain an item of required information, a statement that the item is unknown or cannot be readily obtained may be accepted as a complete reply for that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph should appear in the conclusion of any requirement for information; applicant must still have made reasonable inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding paragraphs and timing (¶¶ 7.125–7.126, 7.127)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the requirement accompanies an Office action, the time for reply to the attached requirement coincides with the Office action period (¶7.125). When mailed without other Office action, the requirement is subject to 37 CFR 1.134, 1.135, and 1.136 and has a shortened statutory period (ordinarily 2 months) (¶7.126). Form paragraph 7.127 should appear at the end of any Office action that includes an attached requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the appropriate concluding form paragraph depending on whether the requirement accompanies an Office action or is mailed alone; allow extensions per 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligation after applicant’s reply (consideration of submitted information)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider the information submitted with the applicant’s reply and apply the information as the examiner deems appropriate; identification of search areas must be considered and the examiner must indicate which areas were and were not used in performing a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indication may be placed in file wrapper search notes or by notations on applicant’s reply with initials/date; for IFW processing see IFW Manual. Answers to queries must be considered and minimally indicated as 'Considered' with initials/date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of art submitted in response to 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Art submitted in response to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement must be considered at least to the extent that art submitted with an Information Disclosure Statement under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 is considered; if applicant provides a written list, examiner must indicate which art has been considered in the same manner as with an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no list is provided, examiner need not prepare a list or make the art of record unless examiner relies on such art in a rejection. It is never appropriate to deny considering information submitted within the scope of a 1.105 requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope criterion for what must be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for measuring the scope of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement is the plain meaning of the text of the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully specify scope in the requirement; information beyond the scope need not be considered unless submitted in conformity with 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 and MPEP §609.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to modify or withdraw 1.105 requirements (¶ 704.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who seek to have a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 withdrawn or modified, or who seek to have information submitted under 1.105 considered, may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.181 is not a reply to the 1.105 requirement; the time period for applicant to reply to the requirement continues to run even if a petition is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between 1.105 replies and Information Disclosure Statements (¶ 704.14(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial reply, if responsive and timely, does not have to satisfy the fee and/or certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98; applicant should list the references on Form PTO/SB/08 to have citations entered in the record. Any replies subsequent to the initial reply must meet provisions of 1.97 and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of art beyond the scope of a 1.105 requirement is treated as a submission under 1.97/1.98 and must meet those provisions for the art to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on making next Office action final after 1.105 reply (¶ 705.01(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in a reply to a 1.105 requirement, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes practice after a 1.105 reply from practice following an IDS under 1.97/1.98; examiners should avoid making reliance-final actions unless fully necessitated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Report (P.R.) use — extraordinary circumstances only (¶ 705.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability Report practice is to be used only in extraordinary circumstances where an application contains claims classifiable in other Technology Centers that are not divisible from claims governing the application's classification; P.R. is signed by the primary examiner in the reporting TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.R. practice should be resorted to only where it will save total examiner time or improve quality due to specialized knowledge; ordinarily not used when a single examiner can complete examination more quickly and adequately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and contents of Patentability Report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patentability Report is in memorandum form and will include citation of all pertinent references and a complete action on all claims involved; the field of search covered should be endorsed on the file wrapper by the examiner making the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the reporting examiner believes final action is in order as to the referred claims, they should so state; if the primary examiner in the TC of jurisdiction agrees, incorporate substance into action; otherwise, consult or remove the P.R. as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Patentability Reports are not proper (exemplary situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: P.R. is ordinarily not proper where claims are related as a manufacturing process and a product defined by the process; where claims are related as product and process that merely makes the product; or where claims are related as a combination and a subcombination (per se) — the examiner having jurisdiction can usually give a complete examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use P.R. where claims differ only in scope or where one examiner can efficiently examine both aspects; P.R. only when it will save total examiner time or improve quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting and approving Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: When primary examiners in both requesting and requested TCs agree a P.R. is necessary and the TC Director of the requesting TC approves, the application is forwarded with a memorandum requesting 'For Patentability Report from TC -- as to claims --.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval should be stamped 'Approved' on the memorandum; for IFW processing follow IFW Manual guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling disagreements and appeals involving P.R.
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner in the receiving TC does not agree with the P.R., they may consult; if agreement cannot be reached, the jurisdictional examiner need not rely on the P.R. and may make their own action, removing the P.R. If an appeal is taken where claims are examinable in the reporting TC and application otherwise allowable, formal transfer for appeal only may be made to the reporting TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On allowance the application may be sent to issue by the appropriate TC with classification determined by controlling claims; notify reporting TCs upon allowance or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of examination and supervisory coordination for P.R.
rubrics_metrics.description: If supervisory examiners cannot agree on order of examination by TCs, the supervisory examiner having jurisdiction will direct that a complete search of the art relevant to his/her claims be made prior to referral; the results should be furnished to the TC receiving the referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order of search may be modified where supervisors find a different sequence expedient; ensure timely reminders to reporting TC to maintain reported dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate prints of drawings for P.R. and file handling
rubrics_metrics.description: In P.R. cases having drawings, the assigned examiner will furnish prints of relevant drawing sheets to the reporting TC for interference search purposes and indicate that this has been done on the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When application with P.R. prosecution is passed for issue or abandoned, notify each TC that submitted a P.R.; reporting TC examiners should note date of allowance or abandonment on duplicate prints; prints may be destroyed when no longer needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews in P.R. cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If an interview is held on an application in which a P.R. has been adopted, the reporting Technology Center may be called on for assistance at the interview when it concerns claims treated by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow general interview guidance in MPEP §§ 713–713.10 regarding participation and conduct of interviews.
